coverage.main: Read all ten pages of arXiv 1904.05181v2 (28 June 2019): Sections 1-5, Algorithms 1-2, Figures 1-4, Tables 1-5 and references. The ACM MM version of record was not retrieved.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or referenced.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 2-4 and Figure 4 report success rates and average query counts of V-BAD, P-BAD and SR-BAD. These are score-based query attacks on the target video model (I3D, CNN+LSTM) with up to 3x10^5 queries. ImageNet image models (ResNet50, DenseNet121/169) supply only tentative perturbations that are then rectified by querying the target. Table 5 reports cosine similarity between tentative/rectified perturbations and the true gradient, a gradient-alignment diagnostic. No zero-query transfer rate from image models to a video model is reported.

f1.evidence: Test accuracies of both video models on all three datasets are reported, positive setup evidence, but no transferred-example evaluation exists.

f2.evidence: One correctly classified test video per category is attacked by querying the target; no transfer denominator exists.

f3.evidence: Success is defined for the query attack within the query limit; there is no source-to-target transfer step.

f4.evidence: Counts would concern query-attack success, not transfer.

f5.evidence: An explicit L-infinity bound epsilon = 0.05 per frame is stated for the query attacks, recorded as positive setup evidence; no transfer result exists to which the field applies.

f6.evidence: An author-named repository exists, but with no transfer configuration it is neither a transfer recomputability success nor a failure.

artifact_checks.result: Found by GitHub search (description matches the paper title; owner name matches the first author; last push 28 October 2019). Not linked in the arXiv text; not cloned or executed; not evaluated as a transfer artifact.

bounds_exclusion.reason: Only query-attack success rates on the attacked target are reported; there is no transferred misclassification rate.

limitations: Transfer-prior query attacks are classified as out of scope, consistent with rank 19; an independent recoder could flag this boundary.
